title: Class syntax and constructors
learningObjectives: Explain class syntax and constructors and choose suitable object-oriented patterns.

understand.concept: JavaScript class syntax provides a structured way to define constructors and prototype methods. A class constructor runs when new creates an instance. Class bodies execute in strict mode, and calling a class without new throws a TypeError.
understand.whyItMatters: Classes can make related instance behaviour easier to organise. They still use JavaScript's prototype system, and simple objects or functions may be more suitable for small data structures.
understand.analogy: A class is a readable blueprint that defines how instances are initialised and which methods they share.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript object identity, prototypes, and class semantics are defined by the language.

explain.narrative: The constructor assigns instance data; describe is defined on Course.prototype and shared by instances.

examples.explanation: The constructor assigns instance data; describe is defined on Course.prototype and shared by instances.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the object creation or class behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Add a constructor parameter with a default value and a prototype method. Create two instances and compare their own properties.
practise.independentTask: Model a small domain using the simplest suitable object pattern. Explain the trade-offs between plain objects, functions, prototypes, and classes.
hints: Separate instance data from shared behaviour.
Check own properties and inherited properties.
Prefer composition when capabilities need to vary independently.

questions.prompt: Where is a normal class instance method defined?
questions.explanation: Class methods are installed on the class's prototype.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between a plain object, function, and class?
options: The actual data and behaviour requirements
A rule that every object must be a class
The number of lines in the file name
questions.answer: The actual data and behaviour requirements
questions.explanation: Choose the least complex abstraction that clearly expresses the required behaviour.
